claim: In beating cardiomyocytes, synchronized localized Ca2+ transients from thousands of active excitation-contraction coupling sites (ECC couplons) comprising plasma and sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane calcium channels are important determinants of the heart's performance.
source: In beating cardiomyocytes, synchronized localized Ca2+ transients from thousands of active excitation-contraction coupling sites (ECC couplons) comprising plasma and sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane calcium channels are important determinants of the heart's performance.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific understanding about cardiac physiology, drawing from general knowledge in the field.

claim: Knowledge about the properties of ECC couplons is limited by the lack of appropriate experimental and analysis strategies.
source: Nevertheless, our knowledge about the properties of ECC couplons is limited by the lack of appropriate experimental and analysis strategies.
evidence: This is an assertion about the state of the field, supported by the authors' inference from existing literature.

claim: CaCLEAN was designed to untangle the fundamental characteristics of ECC couplons by combining the astronomer's CLEAN algorithm with known properties of calcium diffusion.
source: We designed CaCLEAN to untangle the fundamental characteristics of ECC couplons by combining the astronomer's CLEAN algorithm with known properties of calcium diffusion.
evidence: This describes the methodology developed in this study, supported by the data and methods presented in the manuscript.

claim: CaCLEAN empowers the investigation of fundamental properties of ECC couplons in beating cardiomyocytes without pharmacological interventions.
source: CaCLEAN empowers the investigation of fundamental properties of ECC couplons in beating cardiomyocytes without pharmacological interventions.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data showing analysis of ECC couplons in intact cells without drugs.

claim: Individual ECC couplons at the nanoscopic level show decreasing firing reliability during the negative amplitude-frequency relationship.
source: Upon examining individual ECC couplons at the nanoscopic level, we reveal their roles in the negative amplitude-frequency relationship and in β-adrenergic stimulation, including decreasing and increasing firing reliability, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 3 showing changes in firing reliability with stimulation frequency.

claim: Individual ECC couplons at the nanoscopic level show increasing firing reliability during β-adrenergic stimulation.
source: Upon examining individual ECC couplons at the nanoscopic level, we reveal their roles in the negative amplitude-frequency relationship and in β-adrenergic stimulation, including decreasing and increasing firing reliability, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 3 showing changes in firing reliability with isoproterenol treatment.

claim: CaCLEAN combined with 3D confocal imaging of beating cardiomyocytes provides a functional 3D map of active ECC couplons with on average 17,000 per myocyte.
source: CaCLEAN combined with 3D confocal imaging of beating cardiomyocytes provides a functional 3D map of active ECC couplons (on average, 17,000 per myocyte).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from 3D reconstruction experiments presented in Figure 4.

claim: Voltage-operated L-type Ca2+ channels (LTCCs) in the plasma membrane evoke a brief Ca2+ influx during cellular action potentials.
source: During cellular action potentials, voltage-operated L-type Ca2+ channels (LTCCs) in the plasma membrane evoke a brief Ca2+ influx that is amplified by ryanodine receptors (RyRs) in the membrane of the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR).
evidence: This is established knowledge about cardiac excitation-contraction coupling, supported by citation to Bers, 2002.

claim: Ca2+ influx through LTCCs is amplified by ryanodine receptors (RyRs) in the membrane of the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
source: During cellular action potentials, voltage-operated L-type Ca2+ channels (LTCCs) in the plasma membrane evoke a brief Ca2+ influx that is amplified by ryanodine receptors (RyRs) in the membrane of the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR).
evidence: This describes the Ca2+-induced Ca2+ release mechanism, supported by citation to Bers, 2002.

claim: The process of Ca2+ influx amplification by RyRs is referred to as Ca2+-induced Ca2+ release (CICR).
source: This process is referred to as Ca2+-induced Ca2+ release (CICR) (Bers, 2002).
evidence: This is established terminology in the field, supported by citation to Bers, 2002.

claim: LTCCs and RyRs are clustered on their respective membranes and oppose each other to build up the functional excitation-contraction coupling (ECC) unit, the ECC couplon.
source: It is generally accepted that LTCCs and RyRs are clustered on their respective membranes and oppose each other strongly to build up the functional excitation-contraction coupling (ECC) unit, the so-called ECC couplon (Soeller et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citation to Soeller et al., 2007.

claim: Reliable communication between LTCCs and RyRs ensures robust functional coupling of the plasma and SR membranes for each heartbeat.
source: For each heartbeat, reliable communication between these partners ensures robust functional coupling of the plasma and SR membranes and enables synchronized activation of ECC couplons throughout the myocyte, a prerequisite for optimal contractility of the cell (Wier and Balke, 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge about cardiac physiology, supported by citation to Wier and Balke, 1999.

claim: Synchronized activation of ECC couplons throughout the myocyte is a prerequisite for optimal contractility of the cell.
source: For each heartbeat, reliable communication between these partners ensures robust functional coupling of the plasma and SR membranes and enables synchronized activation of ECC couplons throughout the myocyte, a prerequisite for optimal contractility of the cell (Wier and Balke, 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge about cardiac physiology, supported by citation to Wier and Balke, 1999.

claim: Many processes contribute to the dynamics of Ca2+ cycling in cardiomyocytes, including the opening of LTCCs, the activity of SERCA, and the functional state of RyRs.
source: Many processes contribute to the dynamics of Ca2+ cycling in cardiomyocytes, including the opening of LTCCs, the activity of the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase (SERCA) and the functional state of RyRs (Bers, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about cardiac Ca2+ handling, supported by citation to Bers, 2008.

claim: The adrenergic hormone system is a major regulator of minute-by-minute cardiovascular function.
source: The adrenergic hormone system is a major regulator of minute-by-minute cardiovascular function (Dorn, 2010) and evokes activation of the cAMP/protein kinase A signalling pathway, resulting in the phosphorylation of key proteins of ECC, including LTCCs, phospholamban, and RyRs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cardiovascular physiology, supported by citation to Dorn, 2010.

claim: The adrenergic hormone system evokes activation of the cAMP/protein kinase A signalling pathway, resulting in the phosphorylation of key proteins of ECC, including LTCCs, phospholamban, and RyRs.
source: The adrenergic hormone system is a major regulator of minute-by-minute cardiovascular function (Dorn, 2010) and evokes activation of the cAMP/protein kinase A signalling pathway, resulting in the phosphorylation of key proteins of ECC, including LTCCs, phospholamban, and RyRs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about adrenergic signaling, supported by citation to Dorn, 2010.

claim: The adrenergic system results in an increased cellular Ca2+ transient and in cellular force production, fostering the mechanical output of the heart and providing a positive inotropic response.
source: Ultimately, the system results in an increased cellular Ca2+ transient and in cellular force production, fostering the mechanical output of the heart and thus providing a positive inotropic response (Bers, 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge about adrenergic effects on the heart, supported by citation to Bers, 2002.

claim: β-adrenergic stimulation in vivo exerts a positive chronotropic effect.
source: In addition, β-adrenergic stimulation in vivo exerts a positive chronotropic effect, highlighting the importance of understanding the force-frequency response as an important physiological mechanism regulating cardiac output (Anderson et al., 1973).
evidence: This is established knowledge about adrenergic effects on heart rate, supported by citation to Anderson et al., 1973.

claim: Small rodents (e.g., rat and mouse) exhibit a negative force-frequency relationship.
source: As part of the negative force-frequency relationship found in small rodents (e.g., rat and mouse), the amplitude of the global Ca2+ transient decreases with increasing stimulation frequency (Sipido et al., 1998; Gattoni et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about rodent cardiac physiology, supported by citations to Sipido et al., 1998 and Gattoni et al., 2016.

claim: In small rodents, the amplitude of the global Ca2+ transient decreases with increasing stimulation frequency.
source: As part of the negative force-frequency relationship found in small rodents (e.g., rat and mouse), the amplitude of the global Ca2+ transient decreases with increasing stimulation frequency (Sipido et al., 1998; Gattoni et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about rodent cardiac physiology, supported by citations to Sipido et al., 1998 and Gattoni et al., 2016.

claim: Several different processes might contribute to the negative force-frequency relationship, including a decreased SR-Ca2+ content, a decreased number of 'participating' ECC couplons and decreased Ca2+ release from individual ECC couplon sites.
source: Several different processes might contribute to this behavior, including a decreased SR-Ca2+ content, a decreased number of 'participating' ECC couplons and decreased Ca2+ release from individual ECC couplon sites, all of which are able to diminish the global, cellular Ca2+ transient.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential mechanisms, based on inference from existing knowledge.

claim: Whether and to what degree the reliability of couplons' firing adds to the negative force-frequency relationship remains elusive.
source: Whether and to what degree the reliability of couplons' firing adds to the latter contributor remains elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in knowledge that the study aims to address.

claim: Current knowledge of RyR cluster behavior has substantially increased following the advent of confocal microscopy.
source: The current knowledge of RyR cluster behavior has substantially increased following the advent of confocal microscopy, which enables the study of spontaneous, local Ca2+ release signals, the Ca2+ spark (Cheng et al., 1993; Lipp and Niggli, 1994; Cheng and Lederer, 2008).
evidence: This is a statement about the history of the field, supported by citations to key papers on Ca2+ sparks.

claim: Confocal microscopy enables the study of spontaneous, local Ca2+ release signals, the Ca2+ spark.
source: The current knowledge of RyR cluster behavior has substantially increased following the advent of confocal microscopy, which enables the study of spontaneous, local Ca2+ release signals, the Ca2+ spark (Cheng et al., 1993; Lipp and Niggli, 1994; Cheng and Lederer, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about confocal microscopy applications, supported by citations to Cheng et al., 1993; Lipp and Niggli, 1994; Cheng and Lederer, 2008.

claim: ECC couplon sites represent a subset of Ca2+ spark sites and they share similar properties.
source: Although ECC couplon sites represent a subset of Ca2+ spark sites and they share similar properties, their mode of occurrence–i.e., evoked vs. spontaneous, synchronized vs. uncoordinated—disallows direct transfer of Ca2+ spark properties onto those of the couplon site.
evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge about the relationship between Ca2+ sparks and ECC couplons.

claim: The mode of occurrence of ECC couplon sites (evoked vs. spontaneous, synchronized vs. uncoordinated) disallows direct transfer of Ca2+ spark properties onto those of the couplon site.
source: Although ECC couplon sites represent a subset of Ca2+ spark sites and they share similar properties, their mode of occurrence–i.e., evoked vs. spontaneous, synchronized vs. uncoordinated—disallows direct transfer of Ca2+ spark properties onto those of the couplon site.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differences between spontaneous and evoked Ca2+ release events.

claim: Localized Ca2+ transients from ECC couplons occur in a synchronized manner through the action potential and in great numbers (more than ten thousand within a few tens of milliseconds).
source: Localized Ca2+ transients from ECC couplons occur in a synchronized manner through the action potential and in great numbers (more than ten thousand within a few tens of milliseconds) (Bers, 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ECC, supported by citation to Bers, 2002.

claim: The analysis of spontaneous Ca2+ sparks will not capture the properties of ECC couplons following electrical orchestration.
source: The analysis of spontaneous Ca2+ sparks will not capture the properties of ECC couplons following electrical orchestration because spontaneous openings of RyRs might be under the control of different sets of environmental parameters, and because they lack the signal transduction component of translating the electrical action potential into Ca2+ channel opening and into localized Ca2+ influx.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differences between spontaneous and evoked Ca2+ release.

claim: Spontaneous openings of RyRs might be under the control of different sets of environmental parameters compared to evoked openings.
source: The analysis of spontaneous Ca2+ sparks will not capture the properties of ECC couplons following electrical orchestration because spontaneous openings of RyRs might be under the control of different sets of environmental parameters, and because they lack the signal transduction component of translating the electrical action potential into Ca2+ channel opening and into localized Ca2+ influx.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference about RyR regulation.

claim: Spontaneous Ca2+ sparks lack the signal transduction component of translating the electrical action potential into Ca2+ channel opening and into localized Ca2+ influx.
source: The analysis of spontaneous Ca2+ sparks will not capture the properties of ECC couplons following electrical orchestration because spontaneous openings of RyRs might be under the control of different sets of environmental parameters, and because they lack the signal transduction component of translating the electrical action potential into Ca2+ channel opening and into localized Ca2+ influx.
evidence: This is an inference based on the definition of spontaneous vs. evoked Ca2+ release.

claim: The number and arrangement of LTCC and RyR clusters can be determined by appropriate immunohistochemistry.
source: The number and arrangement of LTCC and RyR clusters can be determined by appropriate immunohistochemistry.
evidence: This is established knowledge about immunohistochemistry techniques.

claim: Relating conclusions from immunohistochemistry preparations to the physiological distribution of electrically evoked and functional ECC couplons is rather difficult and often based on many assumptions.
source: However, relating conclusions from such preparations to the physiological distribution of electrically evoked and functional ECC couplons (e.g., by co-localization analysis) is rather difficult and often based on many assumptions.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of immunohistochemistry for studying functional ECC.

claim: Microscopic approaches to studying co-localization, even with super-resolution techniques, are still too coarse to identify functional coupling between LTCCs and RyRs reliably during normal ECC.
source: One of the most striking problems is that microscopic approaches to studying co-localization, even with super-resolution techniques, are still too coarse to identify functional coupling between these two partners reliably during normal ECC.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of current microscopy techniques.

claim: Fixation artefacts, such as shrinking of the preparation or alteration of the nanoscopic arrangement of proteins, might affect co-localization analysis.
source: In addition, fixation artefacts, such as shrinking of the preparation or alteration of the nanoscopic arrangement of proteins, might affect the aforementioned analysis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about potential artifacts in fixed tissue preparations.

claim: Approaches allowing for a robust in situ analysis in the living naive cell during normal ECC are eagerly anticipated.
source: Thus, it clearly follows that approaches allowing for a robust in situ analysis (i.e., in the living naive cell during normal ECC) are eagerly anticipated not only to provide a full appreciation of the physiological 3D distribution of active ECC couplons but also to reveal pathophysiological alterations therein.
evidence: This is an inference about the needs of the field.

claim: The spontaneous firing of individual Ca2+ release clusters (Ca2+ sparks) can technically be monitored by laser-scanning microscopy.
source: The spontaneous firing of individual Ca2+ release clusters, that is Ca2+ sparks, can technically be monitored by laser-scanning microscopy (Cheng et al., 1993; Cheng and Lederer, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Ca2+ spark imaging, supported by citations to Cheng et al., 1993 and Cheng and Lederer, 2008.

claim: The firing of thousands of synchronized but ultra-fast and highly dynamic ECC couplons renders it almost impossible to investigate the behavior of individual ECC couplons during physiological ECC in the absence of pharmacological or experimental interventions.
source: However, the firing of thousands of synchronized but ultra-fast and highly dynamic ECC couplons renders it almost impossible to investigate the behavior of individual ECC couplons during physiological ECC in the absence of pharmacological or experimental interventions such as high Ca2+ buffer concentrations (Cleemann et al., 1998; Woo et al., 2002).
evidence: This is an inference about the technical challenges of studying ECC couplons, supported by citations to Cleemann et al., 1998 and Woo et al., 2002.

claim: The low number of photons per pixel during the brief pixel dwell time and the concomitant high Poissonian noise from the detection device further veil the behavior of individual ECC couplons.
source: Moreover, the low number of photons per pixel during the brief pixel dwell time (effective dwell time down to 50 ns in 2D over time scanning) and the concomitant high Poissonian noise from the detection device (Tian et al., 2012a) further veil the behavior of individual ECC couplons.
evidence: This is an inference about technical limitations of imaging, supported by citation to Tian et al., 2012a.

claim: Microscopic characterization of individual ECC sites in the global population of ECC couplons is akin to the observation of an individual star in a galaxy.
source: Microscopic characterization of individual ECC sites in the global population of ECC couplons is akin to the observation of an individual star in a galaxy.
evidence: This is an analogy used to illustrate the technical challenge.

claim: Mouse atrial myocytes display a complex pattern of Ca2+ signals during normal ECC.
source: As previously reported, mouse atrial myocytes display a complex pattern of Ca2+ signals during normal ECC (Figure 1Aa) (Mackenzie et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1Aa and citation to Mackenzie et al., 2001.

claim: Ultrafast confocal imaging at 147 frames/second allows for the monitoring of complex Ca2+ signals in mouse atrial myocytes.
source: Ultrafast confocal imaging (147 frames/second) allows for the monitoring of such complex Ca2+ signals.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental methods and data presented.

claim: Despite the chance to capture individual time points that display apparent initiation sites of local Ca2+ signals (firing ECC couplons), these are solely 'eager sites', whereas ECC couplons firing later disappear in the evolving global Ca2+ signal.
source: Nevertheless, despite the chance to capture individual time points that display apparent initiation sites of local Ca2+ signals (i.e., firing ECC couplons; see Figure 1Aa – panel 13.7 ms), these are solely 'eager sites' (Mackenzie et al., 2001), whereas ECC couplons firing later disappear in the evolving global Ca2+ signal (see panels in Figure 1Aa later time points).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1Aa and citation to Mackenzie et al., 2001.

claim: Robust de-noising with the CANDLE algorithm, which simultaneously removes Poissonian and Gaussian noise, did not significantly improve the identification of ECC couplons.
source: Robust de-noising with a specialized 'CANDLE' (Coupé et al., 2012), algorithm, which simultaneously removes Poissonian and Gaussian noise, did not significantly improve this situation (Figure 1Ab).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1Ab and citation to Coupé et al., 2012.

claim: The CaCLEAN method enabled identification of active ECC couplons in each of the recorded frames.
source: The CaCLEAN method enabled us to identify active ECC couplons in each of the recorded frames (Figure 1B; for display reasons, we applied a slight blurring to the data; for the original CaCLEAN data, please see Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Fluorescence images rebuilt based on active ECC couplon maps resembled the original fluorescence very closely.
source: When we rebuilt the fluorescence images based on these active ECC couplon maps (Figure 1C), they resembled the original fluorescence very closely (compare Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1C.

claim: There is high similarity between identified release sites and the plasma membrane, with a structural similarity index (SSIM) of 0.56 (average 0.57 ± 0.03, n = 46 from three animals).
source: We overlaid the cumulative active couplon map (Figure 1Da) and the plasma membrane in the same confocal section (Figure 1Db) and observed high similarity between identified release sites and the plasma membrane (Figure 1Dc, the structural similarity index (SSIM) (Wang et al., 2004) was 0.56 with an average of 0.57 ± 0.03, n = 46 from three animals).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of data shown in Figure 1D and citation to Wang et al., 2004.

claim: For CaCLEAN, only the upstroke period of Ca2+ transients was considered, so it was unimportant to capture the 'true' peak of the Ca2+ transient, and contraction of the cardiac myocyte did not affect the determination of the ECC couplon sites.
source: Because for CaCLEAN, we only considered the upstroke period of Ca2+ transients, it was unimportant to capture the 'true' peak of the Ca2+ transient, and contraction of the cardiac myocyte did not affect the determination of the ECC couplon sites (for additional experiments concerning that important aspect, see Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The CaCLEAN algorithm has an apparent z-resolution of approximately 1 µm under the recording conditions used.
source: The peak CaCLEAN signal displayed a decreasing magnitude with an increasing distance to the plane of focus, resulting in an apparent z-resolution of approximately 1 µm under our recording conditions (see Figure 1—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The CaCLEAN algorithm is able to resolve local transients whose centres are 1 µm apart.
source: From these data, we concluded that the CaCLEAN algorithm is able to resolve local transients whose centres are 1 µm apart (Figure 1—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: In rat ventricular myocytes, the mean distance between RyR clusters was reported to be 1.02 µm.
source: In rat ventricular myocytes, the mean distance between RyR clusters was reported to be 1.02 µm (Soeller et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature, supported by citation to Soeller et al., 2007.

claim: There is good correlation between CaCLEAN-calculated maps and simulated maps of Ca2+ release sites.
source: Superimposing the calculated maps with the original simulate maps (Figure 1—figure supplement 6B) demonstrated a good correlation between these two data sets.
evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: The CaCLEAN algorithm neither generated any false positive ECC couplons nor lost any Ca2+ release events in simulations with 1000 randomly distributed events.
source: Superimposing the centres of Ca2+ release with the CaCLEANed couplon map (Figure 1—figure supplement 7E) demonstrated that the CaCLEAN algorithm neither generated any false positive ECC couplons nor lost any Ca2+ release events.
evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 7.

claim: The CaCLEAN algorithm can reproduce the physiological 3D distribution of active ECC couplons throughout rat ventricular myocytes.
source: On the basis of these tests in both the xy-plane and z-axis (Figure 1—figure supplement 4), we believe that the CaCLEAN algorithm can reproduce the physiological 3D distribution of active ECC couplons throughout rat ventricular myocytes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the validation tests shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4 and other supplementary figures.

claim: The relationship between the CaCLEAN signal and the z-position is non-linear, resulting in an augmented functional 'rejection' of 'out of focus' Ca2+ signals and improved sectioning.
source: Interestingly, the relationship between the CaCLEAN signal and the z-position was non-linear (see Figure 1—figure supplement 4), resulting in an augmented functional 'rejection' of 'out of focus' Ca2+ signals and improved sectioning, as displayed in Figure 1E.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4 and Figure 1E.

claim: CaCLEAN transients display a very strong preference (more than 10-fold difference in peak intensity) for 'in focus' signals over those transients alongside the ECC couplon site.
source: Although the pixel Ca2+ signals were comparable at all positions (Figure 1Eb and C), the resulting CaCLEAN transients displayed a very strong preference for the 'in focus' signals over those transients alongside the ECC couplon site (more than 10-fold difference in the peak intensity).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Rebuilt fluorescence transients from the couplon map closely resembled the de-noised original data, indicating that CaCLEAN identified all active couplon sites contributing to the cellular Ca2+ transient.
source: Rebuilt fluorescence transients from the couplon map closely resembled the de-noised original data (compare Figure 1Ec and e), indicating that CaCLEAN identified all active couplon sites contributing to the cellular Ca2+ transient.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of data shown in Figure 1Ec and e.

claim: There is a very good match (correlation coefficient = 0.84 ± 0.008) between three CaCLEAN maps calculated from the same Ca2+ transient with variable noise, supporting the high reproducibility of CaCLEAN calculations.
source: As depicted in Figure 2Ad and e, we found a very good match (correlation coefficient = 0.84 ± 0.008; see Figure 2Af) between the three masks, supporting the high reproducibility of CaCLEAN calculations.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The pattern of active ECC couplons was rather different between two consecutive Ca2+ transients (average correlation coefficient 0.47 ± 0.025) despite superimposable global Ca2+ transients.
source: In the superimposed cellular overview (Figure 2Bc), as well as in the detailed magnified panels (Figure 2Bd, rightmost panel), it became obvious that the pattern of active ECC couplons was rather different between two consecutive Ca2+ transients (average correlation coefficient 0.47 ± 0.025; see Figure 2Bf) despite superimposable global Ca2+ transients (Figure 2Be).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In a typical mouse atrial myocyte, 342 active ECC couplons were identified in the first transient and 352 in the second, but only 215 participated in both Ca2+ transients, indicating a re-fire rate of only 62.8%.
source: We identified 342 active ECC couplons in the first transient and 352 in the second but only 215 that participated in both Ca2+ transients, indicating a re-fire rate of only 62.8%.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of the data.

claim: The firing probability of ECC couplons across four consecutive Ca2+ transients demonstrated that only approximately 10% of couplons were always active.
source: The firing probability of ECC couplons across four consecutive Ca2+ transients demonstrated that only approximately 10% of couplons were always active (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The reliable couplons that fire consistently were probably the eager sites described previously.
source: These reliable couplons were probably the eager sites described previously (Mackenzie et al., 2001).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with previous literature, supported by citation to Mackenzie et al., 2001.

claim: Rat ventricular myocytes display a well-known negative force-frequency relationship.
source: Rat ventricular myocytes display a well-known negative force-frequency relationship (Anderson et al., 1973), resulting, in part, from a decreased amplitude of the global Ca2+ transient with increasing stimulation frequency (Sipido et al., 1998; Gattoni et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about rat cardiac physiology, supported by citations to Anderson et al., 1973; Sipido et al., 1998; and Gattoni et al., 2016.

claim: The negative force-frequency relationship in rat ventricular myocytes results, in part, from a decreased amplitude of the global Ca2+ transient with increasing stimulation frequency.
source: Rat ventricular myocytes display a well-known negative force-frequency relationship (Anderson et al., 1973), resulting, in part, from a decreased amplitude of the global Ca2+ transient with increasing stimulation frequency (Sipido et al., 1998; Gattoni et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge, supported by citations to Sipido et al., 1998 and Gattoni et al., 2016.

claim: Global Ca2+ transients displayed the expected negative amplitude-frequency relationship in rat ventricular myocytes.
source: The resulting global Ca2+ transients displayed the expected negative amplitude-frequency relationship, as depicted in Figure 3Ca.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3Ca.

claim: Isoproterenol substantially increased the Ca2+ transient amplitudes, particularly at low stimulation frequencies.
source: Isoproterenol substantially increased the Ca2+ transient amplitudes, particularly at low stimulation frequencies.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3Ca.

claim: Isoproterenol promoted ECC under both low and high stimulation frequencies (intervals of 600 ms and 150 ms, respectively), albeit to a vastly different degree.
source: Isoproterenol promoted ECC under both the low and high stimulation frequencies (intervals of 600 ms and 150 ms, respectively), albeit to a vastly different degree.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: The average densities of active ECC couplons in control rat ventricular myocytes were 653 ± 148 per 1000 μm2 at 1.7 Hz (600 ms intervals) and 310 ± 146 at 6.7 Hz (150 ms intervals).
source: The resulting average densities of active ECC couplons of the control myocytes were 653 ± 148 per 1000 μm2 (electrical stimulation @ 1.7 Hz; 600 ms intervals) and 310 ± 146 (electrical stimulation @ 6.7 Hz; 150 ms intervals) (Figure 3Cb, filled symbols).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of data shown in Figure 3Cb.

claim: Isoproterenol increased the density of active ECC couplons to 803 ± 35 per 1000 μm2 at 1.7 Hz and 409 ± 185 at 6.7 Hz.
source: Isoproterenol increased the density of active ECC couplons (803 ± 35 per 1000 μm2 [@1.7 Hz] and 409 ± 185 [@6.7 Hz; Figure 3Cb, open symbols]).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of data shown in Figure 3Cb.

claim: Under both control and isoproterenol conditions, the density of recruited ECC couplons dropped monotonically with different quantitative relationships (τctrl=107 ms vs. τiso=80 ms).
source: Under both conditions, the density of recruited ECC couplons dropped monotonically, albeit with a different quantitative relationship (τctrl=107 ms vs. τiso=80 ms).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of the data.

claim: Isoproterenol promoted the released Ca2+ content of each active couplon at low stimulation frequencies by more than 3-fold.
source: In addition to the changes in ECC couplon density, isoproterenol promoted the released Ca2+ content of each active couplon at low stimulation frequencies by more than 3-fold (Figure 3Cc).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of data shown in Figure 3Cc.

claim: The full width at half maximum (FWHM) of ECC couplons displayed small increases following isoproterenol stimulation.
source: The full width at half maximum (FWHM) of these couplons also displayed small increases following isoproterenol stimulation (Figure 3Cd).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of data shown in Figure 3Cd.

claim: Both the Ca2+ release amplitudes of individual couplons and their FWHM followed similar monotonic decay patterns with increasing stimulation frequency.
source: Both the Ca2+ release amplitudes of individual couplons and their FWHM also followed similar monotonic decay patterns with increasing stimulation frequency.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3Cc and d.

claim: The inter-CaT and intra-CaT coefficients of variation (CV) are interpreted as the results of the firing reliability of ECC couplons, with smaller values for CV resulting from 'more homogeneous' active ECC couplon maps.
source: We interpret the inter-CaT and intra-CaT coefficients of variation (CV) as the results of the firing reliability of ECC couplons because smaller values for CV result from 'more homogeneous' active ECC couplon maps.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the CV metric as a measure of reliability.

claim: The data clearly demonstrated a decreasing firing reliability with increases in the stimulation frequency.
source: Our data clearly demonstrated a decreasing firing reliability with increases in the stimulation frequency.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3Ce and f.

claim: For low, physiological stimulation frequencies, application of 10 nM isoproterenol was able to increase temporal and spatial reliability significantly.
source: For the low, physiological stimulation frequencies, application of 10 nM isoproterenol was able to increase temporal and spatial reliability significantly (Figure 3Ce and f).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of data shown in Figure 3Ce and f.

claim: At the highest pacing frequency, β-adrenergic stimulation was unable to increase reliability.
source: Interestingly, again at the highest pacing frequency, β-adrenergic stimulation was unable to increase reliability.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3Ce and f.

claim: CaCLEAN maps closely resembled the expected distribution of ECC couplons in healthy ventricular myocytes with periodic distances of 1.7 μm, as verified by Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis.
source: These ECC couplon maps closely resembled the expected distribution of ECC couplons in healthy ventricular myocytes with periodic distances of 1.7 μm, as verified by a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis (Figure 3Da).
evidence: This is supported by FFT analysis shown in Figure 3Da.

claim: The FFT power of periodic distances in the couplon maps is comparable to the immunostaining results of RyRs.
source: The FFT power of these periodic distances in the couplon maps is comparable to the immunostaining results of RyRs (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of FFT analysis with immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The analysis is not strongly influenced by 'out-of-focus' Ca2+ sources that would disturb and weaken the periodicity (i.e., the power of the spatial frequency).
source: These data also indicate that our analysis is not strongly influenced by 'out-of-focus' Ca2+ sources that would disturb and weaken the periodicity, that is, the power of the spatial frequency.
evidence: This is an inference based on the FFT analysis results.

claim: The power of the characteristic spatial frequency decreases with decreasing stimulation interval, most probably because the failure rate of ECC couplons is increasing.
source: Interestingly, the power of the characteristic spatial frequency decreases with decreasing stimulation interval (Figure 3Db), most probably because the failure rate of ECC couplons is increasing, while the value for the characteristic periodic distance was decreasing at the highest stimulation frequency, probably because of substantial increases in the diastolic Ca2+ concentration (Figure 3Dc).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the FFT data shown in Figure 3Db, with speculation about the mechanism.

claim: The value for the characteristic periodic distance was decreasing at the highest stimulation frequency, probably because of substantial increases in the diastolic Ca2+ concentration.
source: Interestingly, the power of the characteristic spatial frequency decreases with decreasing stimulation interval (Figure 3Db), most probably because the failure rate of ECC couplons is increasing, while the value for the characteristic periodic distance was decreasing at the highest stimulation frequency, probably because of substantial increases in the diastolic Ca2+ concentration (Figure 3Dc).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the FFT data shown in Figure 3Dc, with speculation about the mechanism.

claim: Neither the power of the characteristic spatial frequency nor the characteristic periodic distance relationship was altered in the presence of 10 nM isoproterenol.
source: It was noteworthy that neither of the two latter relationships was altered in the presence of 10 nM isoproterenol (open symbols in Figure 3Db and C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3Db and c.

claim: On average, there were 0.55 couplons/µm3 in rat ventricular myocytes.
source: Figure 4C summarizes the results: on average, there were 0.55 couplons/µm3.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of 3D reconstruction data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Given the typical volume of a rat ventricular myocyte of approximately 30,000 µm3 (n = 15), the average number of active ECC couplons in a typical rat ventricular myocyte was approximately 16,500 couplons.
source: Given the typical volume of a rat ventricular myocyte of approximately 30,000 µm3 (n = 15), the average number of active ECC couplons in a typical rat ventricular myocyte was approximately 16,500 couplons.
evidence: This is calculated from the density measurement and typical cell volume.

claim: The value of approximately 16,500 active ECC couplons per rat ventricular myocyte correlates well with previously reported values.
source: This value correlates well with previously reported values (Bers, 2008).
evidence: This is a comparison with literature values, supported by citation to Bers, 2008.

claim: The heart's pumping performance, measured in vivo as ejection fraction or fractional shortening, is substantially determined by the properties of the underlying cellular Ca2+ transients.
source: The heart's pumping performance, measured in vivo as ejection fraction or fractional shortening, is substantially determined by the properties of the underlying cellular Ca2+ transients.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cardiac physiology.

claim: Cellular Ca2+ signals are the result of brief Ca2+ influxes during the cellular action potential and of the subsequent triggered Ca2+ release from the SR at sites of LTCC-RyR couplings, the so-called ECC couplons.
source: These Ca2+ signals are the result of brief Ca2+ influxes during the cellular action potential and of the subsequent triggered Ca2+ release from the SR at sites of LTCC-RyR couplings, the so-called ECC couplons (Soeller et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge about cardiac ECC, supported by citation to Soeller et al., 2007.

claim: To date, detailed studies of ECC couplon behavior have been restricted to experimental conditions with strong Ca2+ buffering or with substantial inhibition of LTCCs.
source: To date, detailed studies of ECC couplon behavior have been restricted to experimental conditions with strong Ca2+ buffering (Cleemann et al., 1998; Woo et al., 2002), which are thought to uncouple individual ECC couplons during electrically evoked Ca2+ transients, or with substantial inhibition of LTCCs, in which the number of firing ECC couplons is largely suppressed (López-López et al., 1995) (e.g., with verapamil, see Figure 5).
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of previous approaches, supported by citations to Cleemann et al., 1998; Woo et al., 2002; and López-López et al., 1995, and data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Strong Ca2+ buffering is thought to uncouple individual ECC couplons during electrically evoked Ca2+ transients.
source: To date, detailed studies of ECC couplon behavior have been restricted to experimental conditions with strong Ca2+ buffering (Cleemann et al., 1998; Woo et al., 2002), which are thought to uncouple individual ECC couplons during electrically evoked Ca2+ transients, or with substantial inhibition of LTCCs, in which the number of firing ECC couplons is largely suppressed (López-López et al., 1995) (e.g., with verapamil, see Figure 5).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the effects of Ca2+ buffering, supported by citations to Cleemann et al., 1998 and Woo et al., 2002.

claim: Substantial inhibition of LTCCs largely suppresses the number of firing ECC couplons.
source: To date, detailed studies of ECC couplon behavior have been restricted to experimental conditions with strong Ca2+ buffering (Cleemann et al., 1998; Woo et al., 2002), which are thought to uncouple individual ECC couplons during electrically evoked Ca2+ transients, or with substantial inhibition of LTCCs, in which the number of firing ECC couplons is largely suppressed (López-López et al., 1995) (e.g., with verapamil, see Figure 5).
evidence: This is established knowledge, supported by citation to López-López et al., 1995 and data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The detailed properties of fundamental Ca2+ signals from ECC couplons have not been elucidated to date because of several major obstacles: the speed of the Ca2+ release process, the close proximity of numerous ECC couplons, the fast diffusion of Ca2+ ions, and the sheer amount of synchronized ECC couplons.
source: Nevertheless, the detailed properties of such fundamental Ca2+ signals have not been elucidated to date because of several major obstacles: (1) the speed of the Ca2+ release process itself (in the millisecond range [Cheng et al., 1993]); (2) the close proximity of numerous ECC couplons (less than 1 μm in a typical myocyte [Hou et al., 2015]); (3) the fast diffusion of Ca2+ ions (in the range of tens of μm2/s); and (4) the sheer amount of synchronized ECC couplons (many thousands in a typical myocyte) (Bers, 2008).
evidence: This is an inference about the technical challenges, supported by citations to Cheng et al., 1993; Hou et al., 2015; and Bers, 2008.

claim: Substantial noise during ultra-fast Ca2+ imaging adds further complexity to the challenge of identifying active couplons and analyzing their behavior during electrically evoked cellular Ca2+ transients.
source: Substantial noise during ultra-fast Ca2+ imaging adds further complexity to the challenge of identifying active couplons and analyzing their behavior during electrically evoked cellular Ca2+ transients.
evidence: This is an inference about technical challenges in imaging.

claim: In radio astronomy, researchers need to distinguish minute changes in the radio signal from a noisy background and determine the position of such radio sources with high precision.
source: In radio astronomy, researchers need to distinguish minute changes in the radio signal from a noisy background and determine the position of such radio sources with high precision.
evidence: This is established knowledge about radio astronomy.

claim: The CLEAN algorithm was introduced in the 1970s to perform deconvolution on images created in radio astronomy.
source: The CLEAN algorithm was introduced in the 1970s to perform such a deconvolution on images created in radio astronomy (Högbom, 1974).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the CLEAN algorithm, supported by citation to Högbom, 1974.

claim: The CLEAN algorithm assumes that an image consists of a number of point sources for the radio signal and iteratively finds the highest value in the image and subtracts a small representation of this point source convolved with the point spread function until the radio signal has 'disappeared' below a set threshold.
source: Briefly, the algorithm assumes that an image consists of a number of point sources for the radio signal. The algorithm iteratively finds the highest value in the image and subtracts a small representation of this point source convolved with the point spread function (called 'dirty beam' in radio astronomy) of the observatory until the radio signal has 'disappeared' below a set threshold (Pety, 2007).
evidence: This is a description of the CLEAN algorithm, supported by citation to Pety, 2007.

claim: The activity of individual ECC couplons in cardiac myocytes shares substantial similarity with the imaging process in radio astronomy in four key aspects: the global Ca2+ transient is the result of a large number of active ECC sites; the underlying cardiac couplon serves as the point source; the flux of Ca2+ from these ECC couplons serves as the signal-emitting process; and the Ca2+ diffusion process can be readily approximated by the convolution of a light point source with the point spread function.
source: The activity of individual ECC couplons in cardiac myocytes shares substantial similarity with the imaging process in radio astronomy: (1) the global Ca2+ transient is the result of a large number of active ECC sites; (2) the underlying cardiac couplon serves as the point source; (3) the flux of Ca2+ from these ECC couplons serves as the signal-emitting process; and (4) the Ca2+ diffusion process can be readily approximated by the convolution of a light point source with the point spread function.
evidence: This is an analogy drawn by the authors to justify their approach.

claim: The proposed CaCLEAN algorithm is remarkably powerful in deconvolving and identifying active ECC couplons and in determining minute differences in their resulting Ca2+ signals and behaviors such as firing reliability.
source: The results presented in this report strongly suggest that the proposed algorithm is remarkably powerful in deconvolving and identifying active ECC couplons and in determining minute differences in their resulting Ca2+ signals and behaviors such as firing reliability.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Mouse atrial myocytes, with their complex and irregular membrane invaginations, served as a test for evaluating CaCLEAN.
source: Mouse atrial myocytes, with their complex and irregular membrane invaginations (Kirk et al., 2003), served as a test for evaluating CaCLEAN.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach, supported by citation to Kirk et al., 2003.

claim: ECC couplons are restricted to regions in close proximity to membrane invaginations in mouse atrial myocytes.
source: ECC couplons are restricted to regions in close proximity to such membrane invaginations (Kirk et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge about atrial myocyte structure, supported by citation to Kirk et al., 2003.

claim: An overlay of the CaCLEAN-derived couplon positions and the plasma membrane revealed strong structural similarity between these two data sets.
source: Indeed, an overlay of the CaCLEAN-derived couplon positions and the plasma membrane revealed strong structural similarity between these two data sets (see Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The CaCLEAN algorithm helps to discriminate positions at ECC couplon sites from those even a short distance away from such ECC centres.
source: Although Ca2+ transients in the vicinity of couplon sites can still have substantial amplitude (Figure 1Ea), the CaCLEAN algorithm helps to discriminate positions at ECC couplon sites from those even a short distance away from such ECC centres (see Figure 1Ec and Figure 1—figure supplements 4 and 5).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1Ec and supplementary figures.

claim: CaCLEAN also serves functionally as a 'deconvolution' algorithm.
source: Thus, CaCLEAN also serves functionally as a 'deconvolution' algorithm.
evidence: This is an inference based on the algorithm's ability to separate overlapping signals.

claim: The CaCLEAN algorithm displays substantial robustness because it generates virtually identical couplon maps from the same underlying Ca2+ transient convoluted with random but different noise simulating recording parameters.
source: Moreover, the CaCLEAN algorithm displays substantial robustness because it generates virtually identical couplon maps from the same underlying Ca2+ transient convoluted with random but different noise simulating our recording parameters (Figure 2A) and from simulated Ca2+ transients (Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: The two parameters for Ca2+-dye diffusion and the definition of ACO are rather critical for the CaCLEAN algorithm.
source: As depicted in Figure 6, the two parameters for the Ca2+-dye diffusion and the definition of ACO are rather critical.
evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: The optimal values for Ca2+-dye diffusion (60 μm2/s) and ACO (30 μm2/s) yield the best resolution for CaCLEAN.
source: We determined the optimal values for these two parameters (60 μm2/s for Ca2+-dye diffusion and 30 μm2/s for 'Analytical CLEAN Object' [ACO]) yielding the best resolution.
evidence: This is supported by optimization analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: For all three optical axes, CaCLEAN has a resolution of 1 µm, a value that matched the average distance between putative ECC couplon sites well.
source: For all three optical axis, we determined a resolution of 1 µm, a value that matched the average distance between putative ECC couplon sites well (Soeller et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by validation data and citation to Soeller et al., 2007.

claim: Any manoeuvres that improve the signal-to-noise ratio of the recorded data, such as the use of Ca2+ sensors with superior properties, will also help to improve the resolution of CaCLEAN.
source: Any manoeuvres that improve the signal-to-noise ratio of the recorded data, such as the use of Ca2+ sensors with superior properties, will also help to improve the resolution of CaCLEAN.
evidence: This is a speculation about potential improvements to the method.

claim: High concentrations (1–5 mM) of a slow Ca2+ buffer, such as EGTA, have been previously used in rat atrial and ventricular myocytes to identify and investigate the properties of ECC couplon sites.
source: Another approach to characterizing the function of couplon-mediated local Ca2+ transients is employing high concentrations (1–5 mM) of a slow Ca2+ buffer, such as EGTA. This method has been previously used in rat atrial (Woo et al., 2002, 2005) and ventricular myocytes (Zahradníková et al., 2007; Janiek et al., 2012) to identify and investigate the properties of ECC couplon sites.
evidence: This is established knowledge about previous methods, supported by citations to Woo et al., 2002, 2005; Zahradníková et al., 2007; and Janiek et al., 2012.

claim: Results in atrial myocytes from CaCLEAN are in line with previous findings indicating that ECC is restricted to subplasmalemmal regions.
source: Our results in atrial myocytes (Figure 1Dc) are in line with previous findings indicating that ECC is restricted to subplasmalemmal regions (Woo et al., 2002, 2005; Mackenzie et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a comparison with literature, supported by data in Figure 1Dc and citations to Woo et al., 2002, 2005 and Mackenzie et al., 2001.

claim: The report by Woo et al. (2005) in rat ventricular myocytes compared their experimental results to data obtained by modeling the behavior of individual RyR clusters during ECC, allowing for a molecular interpretation of the measured 'Ca2+ spikes'.
source: The report by Woo et al. (2005) in rat ventricular myocytes went a step further and compared their experimental results to data obtained by modeling the behavior of individual RyR clusters during ECC. This strategy allowed for a molecular interpretation of the measured 'Ca2+ spikes' (Janiek et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a description of previous work, supported by citations to Woo et al., 2005 and Janiek et al., 2012.

claim: Results from rat ventricular myocytes using CaCLEAN depicted the described variability of ECC in ventricular myocytes and extends these findings to the negative amplitude-frequency relationship in small rodents.
source: Our results from rat ventricular myocytes (Figure 3Ce and f) also depicted the described variability of ECC in ventricular myocytes and extends these findings to the negative amplitude-frequency relationship in small rodents.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3Ce and f.

claim: Previous approaches using high Ca2+ buffer concentrations relied on patch clamping the cells and using excessive concentrations of a slow Ca2+ buffer that might alter L-type Ca2+ channels and/or RyR gating.
source: Nevertheless, these approaches relied on patch clamping the cells and using excessive concentrations of a slow Ca2+ buffer that might alter L-type Ca2+ channels and/or RyR gating.
evidence: This is an inference about potential limitations of previous methods.

claim: CaCLEAN is able to identify ECC couplons in intact ventricular myocytes with a low concentration of a fast Ca2+ buffer, the Ca2+ sensor.
source: By contrast, CaCLEAN is able to identify ECC couplons in intact ventricular myocytes with a low concentration of a fast Ca2+ buffer, the Ca2+ sensor.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental approach described in the methods and results.

claim: The CaCLEAN algorithm assumes both symmetrical Ca2+-dye diffusion and ACO.
source: The CaCLEAN algorithm assumes both symmetrical Ca2+-dye diffusion and ACO; thus, barrier structures such as mitochondria or the SR itself might result in asymmetrical Ca2+ diffusion.
evidence: This is a description of an assumption in the algorithm.

claim: Barrier structures such as mitochondria or the SR itself might result in asymmetrical Ca2+ diffusion.
source: The CaCLEAN algorithm assumes both symmetrical Ca2+-dye diffusion and ACO; thus, barrier structures such as mitochondria or the SR itself might result in asymmetrical Ca2+ diffusion.
evidence: This is a speculation about potential limitations of the symmetrical diffusion assumption.

claim: The symmetrical ACO does not represent a substantial problem because it is used as an almost nanoscopic component for de-composing the Ca2+ signal in a highly iterative manner.
source: The symmetrical ACO does not represent a substantial problem because it is used as an almost nanoscopic component for de-composing the Ca2+ signal in a highly iterative manner (10−4 of the amplitude of the local Ca2+ transient), but the initial steps in CaCLEAN are challenged by this assumption (see Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference about the impact of the symmetrical ACO assumption, supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The severity of the simplified description of the diffusion process depends on the temporal resolution and the magnitude of asymmetry.
source: The severity of this simplified description of the diffusion process depends on (i) the temporal resolution and (ii) the magnitude of asymmetry.
evidence: This is an inference about factors affecting the accuracy of the algorithm.

claim: Because an a priori estimation of inhomogeneous diffusion is essentially impossible, a high temporal resolution appears to be the only way to minimize the effect of asymmetrical diffusion.
source: Because an a priori estimation of inhomogeneous diffusion is essentially impossible, a high temporal resolution appears to be the only way to minimize this effect.
evidence: This is an inference about how to address limitations of the algorithm.

claim: Despite indistinguishable global Ca2+ transients, the subcellular patterns of firing ECC couplons were substantially different between individual global Ca2+ transients.
source: We were particularly surprised to find that despite indistinguishable global Ca2+ transients, the subcellular patterns of firing ECC couplons were substantially different between individual global Ca2+ transients (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Modulation of the reliability might be an important contributor to variations in the global Ca2+ signal.
source: Therefore, we posited whether the modulation of the reliability might be an important contributor to variations in the global Ca2+ signal.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observed variability in couplon firing patterns.

claim: It was speculated that a number of processes contribute to the negative force-frequency relationship in rat cardiac myocytes, including modulation of the Na+/Ca2+ exchanger activity and the SR Ca2+ content.
source: In rat cardiac myocytes, the negative force-frequency relationship is established (Gattoni et al., 2016), and it was speculated that a number of processes contribute to this negative relationship, including modulation of the Na+/Ca2+ exchanger activity (Yao et al., 1998) and the SR Ca2+ content (Maier et al., 2000; Endoh, 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge and speculation from the literature, supported by citations to Gattoni et al., 2016; Yao et al., 1998; Maier et al., 2000; and Endoh, 2004.

claim: Concomitant to the decreasing amplitude of the global Ca2+ transient, the density of participating ECC couplons substantially decreased with increasing stimulation frequency, as did the amplitude and size of the resulting local Ca2+ transients.
source: We found that concomitant to the decreasing amplitude of the global Ca2+ transient (Figure 3Ca, filled symbols), the density of participating ECC couplons substantially decreased with increasing stimulation frequency, as did the amplitude and size of the resulting local Ca2+ transients (see Figure 3Cc and d).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3Ca, c, and d.

claim: At stimulation frequencies above 10 Hz, the density of active ECC couplons dropped to virtually zero, indicating that the ECC mechanism was no longer able to follow such high pacing frequencies.
source: At stimulation frequencies above 10 Hz, the density of active ECC couplons dropped to virtually zero, indicating that the ECC mechanism was no longer able to follow such high pacing frequencies.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data showing decreased couplon density at high frequencies.

claim: The cut-off frequency or stimulation interval at which ECC couplons fail to fire coincided well with the time of RyR refractoriness.
source: Interestingly, we found in our studies that this cut-off frequency or stimulation interval coincided well with the time of RyR refractoriness (Poláková et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an observation from the data, supported by citation to Poláková et al., 2015.

claim: The reliability of ECC couplons that participate in the global Ca2+ transient was identified as a contributor to the negative Ca2+ transient amplitude-frequency relationship.
source: We were able to identify the reliability of ECC couplons that participate in the global Ca2+ transient as a contributor to the negative Ca2+ transient amplitude-frequency relationship (Figure 3Ce and f).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on data shown in Figure 3Ce and f.

claim: The coefficients of variance for both spatial and temporal reliability were increased two- to four-fold with increasing stimulation frequency.
source: The coefficients of variance for both spatial and temporal reliability were increased two- to four-fold.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of the data.

claim: Spatially synchronized recruitment of ECC couplons following electrical stimulation, an important prerequisite for optimized contractile output of the individual myocyte, was substantially de-synchronized or failing with increasing stimulation frequency.
source: These findings indicated that spatially synchronized recruitment of ECC couplons following electrical stimulation, an important prerequisite for optimized contractile output of the individual myocyte, was substantially de-synchronized or failing with increasing stimulation frequency.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the CV data.

claim: The reliability of ECC couplon recruitment from transient to transient faded as the pacing increased.
source: In addition, the reliability of ECC couplon recruitment from transient to transient faded as the pacing increased.
evidence: This is supported by the inter-CaT CV data.

claim: The failure of spatially synchronous couplon recruitment and recruitment failures between transients are substantial contributors to the ever-decreasing amplitude of global Ca2+ transients with increasing stimulation frequency.
source: From these findings, we conclude that the failure of spatially synchronous couplon recruitment and recruitment failures between transients are indeed substantial contributors to the ever-decreasing amplitude of global Ca2+ transients with increasing stimulation frequency.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data.

claim: β-adrenergic stimulation not only caused more ECC couplons to contribute to the global Ca2+ transient but also caused the global Ca2+ transient to be more homogeneous.
source: Interestingly, β-adrenergic stimulation not only caused more ECC couplons to contribute to the global Ca2+ transient but also caused the global Ca2+ transient to be more homogeneous (Figure 3C), and it is noteworthy that the reliability of consecutively recruiting ECC couplon sites from transient to transient was substantially increased.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The reliability of consecutively recruiting ECC couplon sites from transient to transient was substantially increased by β-adrenergic stimulation.
source: Interestingly, β-adrenergic stimulation not only caused more ECC couplons to contribute to the global Ca2+ transient but also caused the global Ca2+ transient to be more homogeneous (Figure 3C), and it is noteworthy that the reliability of consecutively recruiting ECC couplon sites from transient to transient was substantially increased.
evidence: This is supported by the inter-CaT CV data with isoproterenol.

claim: β-Adrenergic stimulation results in multiple phosphorylation events, including phosphorylation of LTCCs, phospholamban phosphorylation with the de-inhibition of the SERCA pump and direct RyR phosphorylation.
source: β-Adrenergic stimulation results in multiple phosphorylation events, including phosphorylation of LTCCs, phospholamban phosphorylation with the de-inhibition of the SERCA pump and direct RyR phosphorylation (Bers, 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge about β-adrenergic signaling, supported by citation to Bers, 2002.

claim: Phosphorylation of LTCCs evokes an increased Ca2+ trigger for RyR-mediated Ca2+ release.
source: Phosphorylation of LTCCs evokes an increased Ca2+ trigger for RyR-mediated Ca2+ release (Catterall, 2015; Reuter, 1983), whereas phospholamban phosphorylation leads to an increased SR-Ca2+ load that fosters RyR sensitivity towards cytosolic Ca2+ (Tada and Toyofuku, 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge, supported by citations to Catterall, 2015 and Reuter, 1983.

claim: Phospholamban phosphorylation leads to an increased SR-Ca2+ load that fosters RyR sensitivity towards cytosolic Ca2+.
source: Phosphorylation of LTCCs evokes an increased Ca2+ trigger for RyR-mediated Ca2+ release (Catterall, 2015; Reuter, 1983), whereas phospholamban phosphorylation leads to an increased SR-Ca2+ load that fosters RyR sensitivity towards cytosolic Ca2+ (Tada and Toyofuku, 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge, supported by citation to Tada and Toyofuku, 1998.

claim: Direct RyR phosphorylation renders the RyRs more sensitive to cytosolic and/or trigger Ca2+.
source: Moreover, direct RyR phosphorylation also renders the RyRs more sensitive to cytosolic and/or trigger Ca2+ (Marx et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge, supported by citation to Marx et al., 2000.

claim: All of the phosphorylation processes during β-adrenergic stimulation work in synergy and increase the reliability and recruitment of formerly 'silent' couplons.
source: Ultimately, all of these processes work in synergy and increase the reliability and recruitment of formerly 'silent' couplons during β-adrenergic stimulation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined effects of the phosphorylation events.

claim: The three-dimensional distributions of RyRs and LTCCs have been studied extensively.
source: The three-dimensional distributions of RyRs and LTCCs have been studied extensively (e.g., Hou et al., 2015), but to our knowledge, we present the first data on functional 3D maps of active, firing ECC couplons in living ventricular myocytes.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field, supported by citation to Hou et al., 2015.

claim: This study presents the first data on functional 3D maps of active, firing ECC couplons in living ventricular myocytes.
source: The three-dimensional distributions of RyRs and LTCCs have been studied extensively (e.g., Hou et al., 2015), but to our knowledge, we present the first data on functional 3D maps of active, firing ECC couplons in living ventricular myocytes.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the work, supported by the 3D reconstruction data in Figure 4.

claim: 3D functional mapping of ECC couplons in naive cardiac myocytes under steady-state stimulation conditions represents a milestone.
source: We believe that such 3D functional mapping of ECC couplons in naive cardiac myocytes under steady-state stimulation conditions represents a milestone, and will enable further studies investigating the degree and mechanisms of distribution changes under physiological conditions.
evidence: This is an opinion about the significance of the work.

claim: 3D functional mapping of ECC couplons will enable further studies investigating the degree and mechanisms of distribution changes under physiological conditions.
source: We believe that such 3D functional mapping of ECC couplons in naive cardiac myocytes under steady-state stimulation conditions represents a milestone, and will enable further studies investigating the degree and mechanisms of distribution changes under physiological conditions.
evidence: This is a speculation about future applications of the method.

claim: 3D functional mapping can be the basis for further advancements in understanding structural and functional changes or maladaptation of ECC during very early states of cardiac diseases in which minute alterations in the RyR–LTCC relationship occur.
source: Furthermore, these findings can be the basis for further advancements in our understanding of structural and functional changes or maladaptation of ECC during very early states of cardiac diseases in which minute alterations in the RyR–LTCC relationship occur (Gómez et al., 1997).
evidence: This is a speculation about future applications, supported by citation to Gómez et al., 1997.

claim: Most cardiac diseases are accompanied by deterioration of ECC, amongst other mechanisms, by T-tubular remodeling.
source: It is accepted that most cardiac diseases are accompanied by deterioration of ECC, amongst other mechanisms, by T-tubular remodeling (Wei et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge about cardiac disease, supported by citation to Wei et al., 2010.

claim: Functional 3D mapping of active ECC couplons demonstrated strings of coupling sites, most likely alongside T-tubular membrane structures.
source: Our functional 3D mapping of active ECC couplons demonstrated strings of coupling sites, most likely alongside T-tubular membrane structures (Figure 4Bc and d), and thus represents a promising step toward studying the relationship between such functional structures in greater detail.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4Bc and d.

claim: Functional 3D mapping represents a promising step toward studying the relationship between ECC couplons and T-tubular structures in greater detail.
source: Our functional 3D mapping of active ECC couplons demonstrated strings of coupling sites, most likely alongside T-tubular membrane structures (Figure 4Bc and d), and thus represents a promising step toward studying the relationship between such functional structures in greater detail.
evidence: This is a speculation about future applications of the method.

claim: The CaCLEAN algorithm fuses the techniques of classical radio astronomy to knowledge about the biophysics of the cardiac ECC process to empower the identification, mapping and characterization of fundamental ECC coupling sites (couplons) in individual Ca2+ transients from intact cardiac myocytes without pharmacological intervention.
source: The CaCLEAN algorithm fuses the techniques of classical radio astronomy to knowledge about the biophysics of the cardiac ECC process to empower the identification, mapping and characterization of fundamental ECC coupling sites (couplons) in individual Ca2+ transients from intact cardiac myocytes without pharmacological intervention.
evidence: This is a summary of the method and its capabilities, supported by the experimental data.

claim: For the first time, 3D maps of the distribution of active ECC couplons for naïve cardiac myocytes have been constructed.
source: As such, we have been able to construct, for the first time, 3D maps of the distribution of active ECC couplons for naïve cardiac myocytes.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the work, supported by the 3D reconstruction data in Figure 4.

claim: Experimental results from CaCLEAN analyses will further advance understanding of the physiological, as well as the pathophysiological, behavior of ECC couplons and their contribution to clinical conditions such as cardiac arrhythmia.
source: Experimental results from such analyses will further advance our understanding of the physiological, as well as the pathophysiological, behavior of these essential building blocks and their contribution to clinical conditions such as cardiac arrhythmia.

claim: The CaCLEAN approach will also be applicable to Ca2+ signalling in other cell types such as neurons, where the properties of fundamental Ca2+ signals such as those at synapses appear to be instrumental to their cellular and network processing of information.
